messages.content: The sky appears blue because of Rayleigh scattering. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and tiny particles. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than other colors, so it gets scattered in all directions much more than colors like red or yellow. This scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all parts of the sky, making it appear blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere to reach you, scattering away most of the blue and leaving the warmer reds and oranges.
